application.name: orOS
application.summary: A whole desktop in your pocket: over 100 offline apps and games in one place
application.desc:
orOS is a small operating system that runs in a web page: an app menu, a top bar, notifications and more than 100 apps and games, all in English and Greek.
Office apps for everyday work: To-Do, Kanban, Notes, Calendar, Contacts, Writer, Spreadsheet, Mind Map, Wiki and more. Personal apps such as Mood, Habits and One-Sentence Diary, tools such as Calculator, Files and Time, and dozens of games, from Sudoku and Chess to 2048 and Solitaire.
The apps work together: one search box in the menu finds apps and your data, birthdays from Contacts and Kanban due dates show up in Calendar, and a mind map branch can become a To-Do list or a set of slides.
Everything lives on your device and every app has its own help pages, also offline. Every app can also be installed on its own, as a single app with its own icon.
The Android app adds phone features: your orOS contacts and calendar appear in the phone's own Contacts and Calendar apps, reminders arrive as notifications, home-screen widgets and shortcuts open apps directly, and you can share text, links and files to orOS from any app.
Works offline, with no account, no ads, no cookies and no tracking. Sync is optional and end-to-end encrypted, using your own Dropbox.
The app's content updates by itself from useoros.online; a new APK only comes when the Android shell changes. Free and open source (MIT), free forever.

application.desc:

Folders can sit inside folders as deep as you like. Search looks through titles, addresses, descriptions, tags and folder names, tags filter the list with one tap, and you can sort by recent, title or most visited.
Save a readable copy of an article to read later, even offline. Tidy up checks your links for broken or moved pages when you ask, and finds duplicates to merge.
Import bookmarks from your browser or from Pocket, Instapaper, wallabag, Raindrop.io, Linkwarden, linkding or Pinboard, and export them as a standard HTML file. Site icons are never downloaded, so opening the list contacts no websites.
Works offline, with no account, no ads, no cookies and no tracking. Sync is optional and end-to-end encrypted, using your own Dropbox.

orOS Calculator is an everyday calculator with five modes. Standard has memory keys, percentages and Ans; Scientific has brackets, powers and roots, trigonometry in degrees, radians or gradians, logarithms, factorials, constants and many functions.
Graphing draws up to four functions at once. Drag and pinch to explore, trace a curve, and see the roots, lowest and highest points and where two curves cross.
Programmer works in hex, decimal, octal and binary at 8 to 64 bits, with AND, OR, XOR, NOT and shifts, and lets you flip single bits. Finance adds VAT, percentage change, loan instalments with a month-by-month table and savings growth.
Type units and currencies right in the line, such as 3 ft to cm or 20 EUR to USD. A history keeps your results and exports to CSV, and a playful Troll mode is there for fun.

Log calls, emails, meetings, messages and notes, and plan follow-ups with a day and a time. The Agenda shows what is late, what is due today and what is coming, with reminders. Tags, filters and a Not contacted list make sure nobody is forgotten.
Track deals through a pipeline with stages, values, chances and expected close dates, and adapt the stages to your work. The dashboard shows your open pipeline, what you won this month and this year, your win rate and what customers still owe.
Start an invoice or a quote for a customer in one tap, see follow-ups in orOS Calendar and Today, and import customers from CSV, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Invoice Ninja or Odoo. An optional contact form for your website turns messages into new leads, encrypted until CRM picks them up.

orOS Cycle is a quick, private log of your periods, symptoms and pain relief. Log a day in seconds: start or end a period, set the flow of each day, tap the symptoms that apply and note what you took for the pain, with the time.
A timeline shows your periods, and the app estimates when the next one is due from your own averages. Insights show your average cycle and period length, your most frequent symptoms and a report for your doctor. Optional reminders tell you when your period is expected or seems late.
If you want, log your basal body temperature and cervical mucus: the app finds the temperature rise and the mucus peak and shows an estimate of your fertile window, with a chart of the cycle. It is an estimate for body awareness, not contraception and not medical advice.
Bring your history from drip., Clue, Flo or a CSV file. Make your own symptom and medication chips, and rename or delete the ready ones.

My days shows a month calendar with the emoji of each day and finds any line by search; Year shows a whole year on one page to print. A streak keeps you going, an optional evening reminder comes on days with no line yet, and a PIN lock keeps the diary private on this device.
Make a PDF book of a year, export your lines as text, CSV or JSON, and import from Day One, Journey, Diaro and Daylio.

application.name: orOS Drive
application.summary: Back up phone folders to your encrypted orOS Vault, with Dropbox or Nextcloud
application.desc:
orOS Drive keeps folders of your phone in your encrypted orOS Vault, the same Vault the orOS apps and the orOS Drive desktop app use.
Sign in with your own Dropbox, your own Nextcloud, or any WebDAV server that keeps exact ETags. Everything is encrypted on the phone with your sync passphrase before it leaves it; the cloud only sees encrypted pieces.
Pick folders to back up: they are synced in the background, by default only on Wi-Fi. A file you delete on the phone goes to the app's Trash first, and nothing is ever deleted because the cloud looked empty.
The whole orOS disk appears in Android's Files app and in every file picker as "orOS": files download only when you open them, and changes you save go back to the Vault. The app also has its own simple file browser.
No account with us, no ads, no trackers. Free and open source (MIT), free forever.

Preview pictures, PDFs and Markdown, and edit text files with a live Markdown preview. The grid view shows thumbnails of your photos and of the first page of PDFs. Search names, or also the contents of text files and PDFs, in a folder and all its subfolders.
Pack files and folders into a ZIP file and unpack ZIP files, and send documents and spreadsheets to the orOS Converter in one tap.
If you like, connect your Dropbox to browse it, copy or move files into the encrypted orOS disk, and send ordinary copies back to Dropbox to share them.

Habits can be daily, on chosen weekdays, on any day, or a number of times per week or per month. Skip a day when you are sick or away without breaking the streak, add a short note to a day, and set a reminder time.
Each habit shows its current streak and a strength score that grows as you keep it and falls slowly when you miss. Its details show the strength over time, a year of days and your notes. See your week as a list, a whole month as a calendar, and stats with check-offs, perfect days and completion rates.
Bring your habits and their history over from Loop Habit Tracker, Habitica, Streaks, Habitify or any CSV file.

Keep a list of your medicines with their doses and times. The app reminds you of each dose, counts what is left so you know when to refill, shows how regularly you took them, and lets you log symptoms.
Charts show 7 days to a year, with the target range shaded and morning and evening blood pressure apart. A tidy report for your doctor prints or saves as PDF, or as a spreadsheet (CSV).
The Record keeps your Medical ID for emergencies (full screen, with a QR code and a printable wallet card), your appointments, vaccines and documents such as lab results. You can import readings from Withings, OMRON connect, Samsung Health and Apple Health exports.
Health records; it does not diagnose and it is not medical advice.

The dashboard shows what you invoiced and collected, what is outstanding and overdue, a bar per month, your top clients and the VAT per rate. Client statements, polite payment reminders, templates and recurring invoices save time, and you can keep more than one business profile.
Due dates show in orOS Calendar and Today, and Invoices works together with Timesheet, CRM, Quote and Budget. Greek ΑΦΜ, ΔΟΥ and myDATA records are supported; nothing is sent to ΑΑΔΕ unless you connect a provider and press Send.

orOS Kanban helps you follow work from start to finish: cards move across columns such as To Do, Doing and Done, and you can keep one board per project.
Drag cards and columns with a mouse or a finger. Each card has notes, a due date, labels, subtasks with progress, your own extra fields, attachments and a cover. Columns can have work-in-progress limits and rules that run when a card arrives.
See the same board as columns, as a sortable table or on a timeline of days, and split it into swimlanes by label or lane. Search and filter by label, use templates, and archive finished boards. Cards with a due date also show up in the orOS Calendar.
Import boards from Trello, Asana, Jira, ClickUp, WeKan, Planka and Kanri, and export a board as a file or the cards as CSV.

application.name: orOS Mail
application.summary: Read and send email from any IMAP account, with rules, snooze and OpenPGP
application.desc:
orOS Mail reads and sends your email from any provider that offers IMAP. Add up to 10 accounts, browse your folders with their unread counts, see all inboxes together, and read messages offline once they have been opened. Replies are grouped into conversations.
Search the open folder on the device or on the server, snooze messages until later, star, archive, move and block senders, and let rules sort new mail for you. On servers with Sieve, your rules and an out-of-office reply can run on the server itself.
Write with formatting, templates, signatures and attachments, undo a send within a few seconds, schedule a message for later and keep drafts on the server. Messages written offline wait in the Outbox. OpenPGP signs and encrypts mail, and your keys stay on your device.
Pictures from the internet stay hidden until you allow them, and sender and link checks warn about possible fakes. Unsubscribe from mailing lists, add invitations to orOS Calendar, or turn a message into a task, a note or a contact in other orOS apps.
Keeps your data on your device, with no orOS account, no ads, no cookies and no tracking. Browsers can't talk to mail servers directly, so your mail passes through the open-source orOS mail relay, which keeps nothing. Sync is optional and end-to-end encrypted, using your own Dropbox.

orOS Maps finds places and plans routes by car, bike, on foot or by public transport, with route choices, up to three stops and an arrival time. Start navigation for spoken turn-by-turn directions, lane hints and the speed limit of the road.
Save places in coloured groups, discover restaurants, cafés, pharmacies and sights around you with their opening hours, read Wikipedia articles about nearby places and see open street-level photos.
Record, import and follow GPX tracks, plan a track with its elevation profile, and see a heatmap of where you have been. Download an area as an offline map, so the map and search work with no connection.
Help improve OpenStreetMap with notes, place edits and quick questions in the style of StreetComplete.
Your data stays on your device, with no account, no ads, no cookies and no tracking. Maps, search and routes come from free, open services built on OpenStreetMap (such as OSRM, FOSSGIS, Photon and Transitous for public transport); they receive only the places and routes you ask for. Add children and siblings with a tap, drag a node to move its whole branch, fold branches, and give ideas an emoji, a colour, a note, a link or a small picture. Style shapes and borders, group ideas with boundaries and summaries, and link ideas on different branches.
Arrange a map as a classic map, a map to the right, an org chart, a tree or a timeline. Type quickly in the outline view, search the map, and present it full screen, one branch at a time.
Turn a branch into a To-Do list, a note or a slide deck in other orOS apps. Import from FreeMind, Freeplane, XMind, SimpleMind, MindManager, OPML, Markdown and text, and export to PNG, SVG, Markdown, OPML or JSON.

Insights shows a weekly recap, your goals, plain-language patterns, how you felt, your streak, this week against the last, your habits and activities, a month calendar, a year in pixels and breakdowns by place, person and weekday, with filters and a PDF report.
Rename, reorder or hide feelings and activities, add your own with an emoji and a colour, and set goals such as moving three times a week. Import your history from Daylio, Bearable, eMoods or any CSV file.

Artist pages from open data (MusicBrainz, Wikidata, Wikipedia), mixes made from what you play, a yearly recap and charts from ListenBrainz help you find more music. Connect your own Subsonic, Navidrome, Jellyfin or Funkwhale server, WebDAV, Nextcloud or Dropbox, import M3U, PLS and XSPF playlists or your Spotify export, and send your plays to your own ListenBrainz account if you want.

application.summary: Control orOS Studio on your PC from a phone or tablet: mixer and NULL JSFX
application.desc:
Remote for orOS Studio turns a phone or tablet into a control surface for orOS Studio on your PC.
On the PC, open Studio › Settings › Connect a tablet or phone. In the app, scan the QR code or type the 6-digit code, then press Allow on the PC. You get the transport (play, stop, record, loop, click, tempo, position), every track's fader, pan, mute, solo and record arm, the master, and live meters.
Open a track's effects to see and play the NULL JSFX effects with the same interfaces as on the PC: change any control, switch an effect on or off, add, remove and reorder effects.
On the same Wi-Fi the link is direct; elsewhere it goes through the orOS relay, end-to-end encrypted with the code. The PC must allow each new device. The screen stays on while you control Studio, and the app comes back to the same PC without a new Allow.
No account, no ads, no cookies and no tracking. Nothing of your project is kept on the phone.
